citation.authors: Powe CE, Evans MK, Wenger J, Zonderman AB et al

record.population: 2,085 Black and White adults in Baltimore (Healthy Aging in Neighborhoods of Diversity across the Life Span)
record.design: Cohort with genotyping of vitamin D-binding protein variants
record.finding: Total 25-hydroxyvitamin D was 15.6 ng/ml in Black participants against 25.8 in White. Vitamin D-binding protein was also lower (168 against 337 ug/ml). In people homozygous for the same genotype, bioavailable 25(OH)D was similar (2.9 against 3.1 ng/ml). Bone mineral density was higher in Black participants (1.05 against 0.94 g/cm2).
record.note: Observational. Whether 'bioavailable' levels are the right measure is contested; NEJM published correspondence (the 12 Nov research file cites PMID 24571762, not re-opened).

cited_by.title: Vitamins and supplements: what the NHS says

record.design: Cohort study of total vitamin D, vitamin D-binding protein and bone density
record.finding: Mean total 25(OH)D was 15.6 against 25.8 ng/mL in Black against white participants, and vitamin D-binding protein was 168 against 337 micrograms/mL; Black participants had higher bone mineral density. Genetic variants explained about 79% of variation in the binding protein.
record.note: Reused from the vitamin D entry; this card gives NHS advice, not a verdict on the contested bone-health evidence.
